\CRchapter{60}{Where the Weather Answers}{Days 231–233 · Grain 22–24, Y.H. 813}{Low Kiln, Sill}
\CRepigraph{A question asked over the boards is not a question put to a man. The weather answers it and the price of barley answers after it, and the row stands where it stood. What is set under wool keeps its own count; what is covered is not entered; and a thing gone around is still a thing kept.}{A saying of the Cross, told in the last tend of Grain}

\begin{CRchronicle}{60}
Three days came under the Vail roof without a bell. The house kept its time in the kiln’s four pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand, in the river’s note through the finger’s-width door, in the boards’ four nails, four and a knot. The boy kept the three counts on separate trays, for agreeing them would have wanted a payer and none stood to any. He came into his two hundred and thirty-first day, then the second and the third, six months and fifty-one days to fifty-three, and nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath said any of it over him.

Sella Vail went to the fire before the basket each morning, instructing wool, pot, broom, water and river wind, never the basket. She turned the dressed grain under its wool for damp, spread it thin and gathered it back by the handful; it changed state and gained no figure, counted in glances and by a carrying arm that remembered weight and not cost. Cost-questions at the threshold and the well went to the pot and the weather; a fist’s number from the clay road went back into its sleeve. Her finger lay on the shelf’s front edge so the charcoal stayed unread, her hand shut half over the cold clay jar, and the widow’s mark hung untouched for fifty-three days.

At the kindling Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed and told the wood that six were counted and the next he did not count, setting the knife at the lip of its sill beside Garl’s unforged collector sentence. The sentence about an ear worth more than the debt came to his teeth and stopped at the word that would call the loan; nine stoppings stood, the Seed 16 breath was drawn and not spent, and no collector came up the clay road. Jorra Vail parted dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, withheld the note he knew three turns ahead, kept the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, and held his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence reached the pot.

In the second afternoon an ownerless voice came over the boards: which row had the pot gone quiet on? The weather and the price of barley answered, and the voice went up the terrace with the row standing where it stood. He opened it as a surgeon opens a wound, found no witness at the bottom, and set the second asking beside the first with a finger between the two, for two askings are not one witness. Six times the hand answered, the thirty-seventh through the forty-second; the last held two rhythms across the wall --- through Sella’s counted breath and down on the river’s next low note. Each was filed on the sixth place with no payer named, worth nothing at two inches of air. At the close the file lay open; nothing had been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended.
\end{CRchronicle}
